method: Finding the nth weekday of a month is pure Gregorian calendar arithmetic, so the page never consults the system clock, a time zone or the network. Every date is first reduced to an integer count of days since 1970-01-01 with the era-based civil-date conversion: a year is split into 400-year eras of 146,097 days, the day of the year comes from a 153-day cycle that starts in March, and the leap rule is the Gregorian one — divisible by four, except centuries, except multiples of 400. The ISO weekday is that day count taken modulo seven with Monday as 1, so 1970-01-01 is a Thursday, and the same count inverts back to a calendar date when the Thursday of a week is needed. The first requested weekday in a month is day 1 plus the distance from that month's first weekday to the target, wrapped into 0-6; each later occurrence adds seven days, so the nth occurrence is the first plus 7(n-1). The last occurrence is counted back from the month's final day the same way, which is why it is not always the fifth. A requested fifth occurrence beyond the month's length is refused with the actual count, because only a 29-, 30- or 31-day month in the right alignment holds one. The reverse direction divides (day - 1) by seven and adds one to name the occurrence, and marks a date whose weekday does not return within seven days as the last of the month. The ISO 8601 week comes from the Thursday of the date's own week: the week number counts weeks from 1 January of that Thursday's year, so 1 January 2027 reports 2026-W53. Year input is trimmed and must be one to four digits between 1583 and 9999, the page refusing earlier years rather than pretending to convert them from the Julian calendar; month and weekday accept either their number or their English name. Output is English, with an ordinal suffix, the long date, the ISO week and the day of the year, plus a table of every matching weekday in that month. Nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.

sources.title: International standard date and time notation (Markus Kuhn): ISO 8601 calendar dates and week dates, where week 01 is the week containing the year's first Thursday and each week runs Monday to Sunday
